About: An internal Huawei AI strategy workshop surveying large-model fundamentals, 2024 progress, and the distributed-systems engineering (MoE) behind training at scale. Slides reference Pangu, Tsinghua NICS-efc and CAS / ICT.

03 · Insights

The workshop, topic by topic

A · Why large models work
01

Evolution Pattern of Large Models: Scaling Laws

Large Models strategy · scaling laws & emergence
Power scaling laws
  • Model performance (loss, accuracy) improves linearly as resources (data, parameters, compute) grow exponentially
  • Loss ≈ A·N^(−α) + B·D^(−β) + E, where N = model size and D = data scale
  • Loss-vs-size curves hold across parameter counts
Emergent intelligence — quantity → quality
  • Big data: ≥ 10¹¹ tokens
  • Large compute: ≥ 10³ A100 cards
  • Large parameters: ≥ 10¹¹ parameters
[1] “Evolution Pattern of Large Models: Scaling Laws,” Huawei Large Models Strategy Workshop, 2024.
02

Technical Nature of Large Models: Generative Compression

Large Models strategy · generative compression
Core idea
  • Autoregressive LLM training compresses massive text into a model file (example: Llama 2 70B)
The compression pipeline (corpus → compute → model)
  • Corpus: ~10 TB of mostly-Internet text
  • Compute: ~6,000 GPUs, ~1e24 FLOPs
  • Model: 70B parameters, ~140 GB file
Why it matters
  • Hinton: ‘the essence of deep learning might be compression’
  • Ilya Sutskever: ‘compression may be the essence of LLM learning’
[2] “Technical Nature of Large Models: Generative Compression,” Huawei Large Models Strategy Workshop, 2024.
03

R&D Mode: Big Engineering × Disruptive Innovation

Large Models strategy · R&D operating model
Big engineering
  • Large-scale parameters, large compute, big data, and the training framework
Disruptive innovation
  • Emergent intelligence, architecture, trustworthiness, efficiency
Generalization — the product
  • General tasks, general modalities, general scenarios — toward a world model
  • Challenge: efficiently integrating big engineering with disruptive innovation on one platform
[3] “R&D Mode of Large Models: Big Engineering × Disruptive Innovation,” Huawei Large Models Strategy Workshop, 2024.
B · 2024 progress & the road ahead
04

The Year's Progress: Capability, Context, Trust & Cost

2024 progress · capability · context · trust · cost
Reasoning, math & coding
  • GPT-4o markedly stronger on data, code and discipline tasks (vs GPT-4T, Claude 3 Opus, Gemini Ultra/Pro, Llama 3 400B)
  • Closed-source leaders do better on harder math (primary → college tiers)
Context windows exploded
  • 2k (2022) → 32k+ (2023) → 100k–200k (Claude 3, GPT-4 Turbo) → 2M (KimiChat, Gemini 1.5 Pro) in ~18 months
  • 2M enables full-novel analysis and project-level code — ‘context windows vs memory’
Trust & cost
  • Fewer hallucinations: GPT-4o beats GPT-4V on HallusionBench (still open for multimodal)
  • Cheaper & faster: GPT-4o 2× faster / 50% cheaper; Gemini 1.5 Flash 3× faster / up to 90% cheaper; cost ~$0.2–30 per 1M tokens
[4] “Progress of Large Models in 2024: Capability, Context, Trust and Cost,” Huawei Large Models Strategy Workshop, 2024.
05

Future Outlook of Large Multi-Modality Models

2024 progress · toward world models
Three future directions
  • Accurate perception of long-form content (e.g. understanding a two-hour movie)
  • More modalities — from language / vision / audio to science: protein, DNA (AlphaFold)
  • A complete world model — dynamic multi-modal modeling and prediction
[5] “Future Outlook of Large Multi-Modality Models,” Huawei Large Models Strategy Workshop, 2024.

Open-Source Reference Point: InternLM2

open-source reference · InternLM2
Models
  • 7B: beats same-size open-source models, surpassing Google Gemma
  • 20B: handles complex scenarios; rivals GPT-3.5 on key capabilities
Full-chain open-source toolchain
  • Five stages: data processing, pre-training, fine-tuning, deployment, evaluation
  • Context 20k → 1M, tool calling, strong math / data analysis
  • Repo: github.com/InternLM/InternLM
[6] “Open-Source Reference Point: InternLM2,” Huawei Large Models Strategy Workshop, 2024.
07

Large-Model Evolution vs Biological Intelligence

closing reflections · evolution analogy & efficiency
LM evolution mirrors biology
  • LLM ↔ invertebrates (~500M yrs); multimodal ↔ mammals (~200M yrs); embodied ↔ humans (~3M yrs)
  • Examples: ChatGPT → Gemini / InternMultiModal → RT-2, GR-1, FIGURE
Is vision harder than language?
  • Neurons vision:language ≈ 10:1; vision evolved ~500M yrs vs language ~250k yrs
  • Lifetime info: ~2B words (language) vs ~90T tokens (vision) — do vision modalities have different scaling laws?
Chain-wide co-optimization
  • Innovation spans chip, interconnect, framework, data, model, evaluation, deployment
  • A Chip ↔ Model ↔ Interconnection triangle to maximize full-chain energy efficiency
[7] “Large-Model Evolution vs Biological Intelligence,” Huawei Large Models Strategy Workshop, 2024.
C · Systems: distributed training & MoE
08

From Human Intelligence to AI 2.0

Yu Wang et al. · Tsinghua NICS-efc · AI 1.0 → AI 2.0
Two systems of thought (Kahneman)
  • System 1: fast, automatic, intuitive (perception)
  • System 2: slow, analytical, reasoning (cognition) — from ‘Thinking, Fast and Slow’
AI 1.0 → AI 2.0
  • AI 1.0 (perceptive): dedicated discriminative models (CNN / RNN) — ‘based on fitting’
  • AI 2.0 (cognitive): general generative models; a Transformer-based LLM as the foundation model for general multimodal tasks
[8] Y. Wang et al., “From Human Intelligence to AI 2.0,” Huawei Strategy Workshop (Tsinghua NICS-efc), 2024.
09

Domain-Specific Small Models (Infini-3B)

systems & efficiency · small models that beat LLMs
Small models can surpass LLMs
  • Soft-hardware co-optimization + scenario customization let small models beat larger ones
  • Infini-3B: 3B parameters with 7B-class performance (>50% fewer params); +15% inference vs Llama-2-7B; long context & agents
How
  • Scenario-customized training closes the gap with ultra-large models
  • High-fidelity quantization for cross-platform deployment; edge-cloud collaboration unlocks more apps
[9] “Domain-Specific Small Models (Infini-3B),” Huawei Strategy Workshop, 2024.
10

Accelerating Distributed MoE & the All-to-All Bottleneck

CAS / ICT · NICS-efc · distributed Mixture-of-Experts
MoE in Transformers
  • FFN layers are replaced by MoE layers = gate + experts; each expert is an FFN with distinct parameters
  • The gate selects experts per sample (Top-2 in training, Top-1 in inference); a load-balancing loss keeps experts even
Distributed MoE (hybrid parallelism)
  • Expert parallelism: one unique expert per device; data parallelism replicates the non-expert parameters
  • All-to-all communication sends samples to experts and restores them — equal-sized both ways, the core distributed cost
[10] “Accelerating Distributed MoE (Mixture of Experts),” Huawei Strategy Workshop (CAS / ICT), 2024.
11

Memory Capacity & DLRM Motivation

systems engineering · memory sharding · DLRM
GPU memory is the limit
  • Models far exceed GPU memory (BERT 220MB, Llama-2 13GB, GPT-3 350GB, GPT-4 3.52TB) → shard parameters, optimizer states and gradients
  • All-Gather params before the forward pass, Reduce-Scatter gradients after backward (DeepSpeed, Megatron-LM, HF Transformers)
DLRM recommendation models
  • DLRM mixes categorical + numerical inputs; huge embedding tables force model parallelism
  • Also all-to-all bound (forward & backward); a ‘butterfly shuffle’ and time breakdown show communication dominates compute
[11] “Memory Capacity & DLRM Motivation,” Huawei Strategy Workshop (CAS / ICT), 2024.
04 · Conclusions

Synthesis across the workshop

Trends

  • Two laws anchor LLMs: power-law scaling (L ≈ A·N^−α + B·D^−β + E) and training-as-lossy-compression (10 TB → 140 GB for Llama-2-70B).
  • 2024's gains are measurable: stronger reasoning / math / coding, context 2k → 2M, lower hallucination, inference cost down 50–90%.
  • Distributed all-to-all communication (MoE & DLRM) is the dominant bottleneck; models (GPT-4 ~3.52 TB) far exceed single-GPU memory.

Vision

  • The frontier is multimodal ‘world models’ — scientific modalities (protein / DNA), long-video understanding, embodied AI.
  • A bio-evolution analogy: LLM → multimodal → embodied ≈ invertebrate → mammal → human; vision may have different scaling laws.
  • Domain-specific small models (Infini-3B) + quantization + edge-cloud as a practical efficiency path.

Implications for us

  • Efficiency is a systems problem: chip↔model↔interconnect co-design and distributed-MoE acceleration are the key platform bets.
  • Invest in long-context / memory mechanisms and trustworthiness (hallucination reduction).
  • Treat distributed training (sharding, all-to-all optimization) as first-class for scaling.
